steps.claim: Pure continuous curvature has an ordered energy-gap weak estimate
steps.proof: For continuous fixed-L psh u<=v, delta=v-u>=0 and theta_u=ddc(psi+u). Energy difference is (n+1)^-1 sum_j int delta theta_v^j theta_u^(n-j), hence int delta MA(u)<= (n+1)DeltaE. Put T_j=theta_u^j theta_v^(n-1-j). The smooth-to-continuous Dirichlet form D_T(f,g)=-int f ddc g T is positive/symmetric/CS. Sum_j D_Tj(delta)=int delta(MA(u)-MA(v))<=int delta MA(u)<= (n+1)DeltaE. For a fixed real PL test f=h_A-k_A with continuous psh metrics on common semiample A, D_Tj(f)<=2||f||infty (A.L^(n-1)), independent of u,v, since ddc f=theta_h-theta_k and the two positive mixed measures have that degree. Summing CS gives |int f(MA(v)-MA(u))|<=sqrt(n C_f (n+1)DeltaE). Need write every sign, smooth limit and real-test representation proof precisely; no target chosen yet.

steps.claim: Canonical positive raw-mass pure E1 measure
steps.proof: Extended energy decreases along actual USC decreasing psh nets by the compact continuous-majorant argument from214/216, independent of any singular operator. Defining continuous u_i down u in E1 have finite energy limit, so the weak test estimate makes continuous measures Cauchy on dense PL_R functions. Positivity/raw V and Riesz give positive Radon MA(u). Two approximation nets share max(u_i,v_j) down the same actual u; their ordered energy gaps vanish, proving approximation independence. All-point potential is fixed beforehand. For singular ordered u<=v, use continuous approximants and their maxima down v, then pass the fixed PL estimate to weak limits; same energy-gap estimate follows. This proves weak continuity for arbitrary decreasing E1 nets with E1 endpoint.

steps.claim: Actual E1 mixed operator by finite polarization
steps.proof: Continuous psh convexity follows from rational tensor FS systems plus uniform closure. Continuous energy concavity and decreasing energy limits show every nonempty subset average u_I is an actual E1 potential. Define mixed MA(u_1,...,u_n)=1/n! sum_nonemptyI (-1)^(n-|I|)|I|^n MA(u_I). For any simultaneous continuous decreasing approximants this is precisely the genuine positive continuous mixed operator at each stage. Hence its weak limit is positive of raw mass V, independent of all approximants, and symmetric/affine in curvature slots in the exact fixed-L domain. This is not just a numerical or target-labeled measure.

steps.claim: Every actual E1 test integrable against every mixed output
steps.proof: Shift psi by one constant so w and all u_i and their continuous approximation tails are nonpositive. B=-E>=0. For continuous z=(w+sum_i u_i)/(n+1), concavity gives B(z)<= (B(w)+sum_i B(u_i))/(n+1). The j=n term of B(z) expands in positive curvature factors and -z; its -w times mixed theta_u1...theta_un coefficient is n!/(n+1)^(n+2). Thus int(-w)MA_mixed<=C_n(B(w)+sum_iB(u_i)), C_n=(n+1)^(n+1)/n!. First hold a continuous test w_k fixed and pass curvature approximants weakly; then take w_k down w using increasing-continuous Radon integration on the single mixed limit. Gives finite integrability and pole-nullness for all E1 tests. No arbitrary measurable-net MCT.

steps.claim: The key uniform error for a fixed singular test
steps.proof: For continuous psh u and continuous w_k>=w_j, h_k=(u+w_k)/2>=h_j=(u+w_j)/2. Continuous energy difference positivity gives (n+1)(E(h_k)-E(h_j))>=int(h_k-h_j)MA(h_k). Positivity of the curvature expansion gives MA(h_k)>=2^-n MA(u). Hence int(w_k-w_j)MA(u)<=2^(n+1)(n+1)(E((u+w_k)/2)-E((u+w_j)/2)). Hold continuous u,k fixed, let w_j down actual E1 w. Radon increasing-continuous integration and decreasing energy give the same bound with w. For actual singular u, approximate u continuously; w_k-w is nonnegative LSC, so Radon Portmanteau and both energy limits extend the inequality to its canonical MA(u). Portmanteau on compact Hausdorff Radon spaces must be justified using continuous minorants/inner compact level sets, not assumed from metrizability.

steps.claim: Fixed singular test and joint decreasing-weight convergence
steps.proof: For u_i down u in E1, and continuous w_k down w, the potentials (u_i+w_k)/2 form a decreasing product net down (u+w)/2 in E1. Their energies tend its energy. The error bound is uniformly small for i,k on a common tail because E((u_i+w)/2)>=E((u+w)/2). Fixed k tests pass through weak MA convergence, and w_k-w is LSC for the limit-measure Portmanteau bound, giving int w MA(u_i)->int w MA(u). For actual E1 weights w_i down w, compact USC superlevels against any fixed continuous w_k give w_i<=w_k+epsilon on a tail. Then 0<=int(w_i-w)MA(u_i)<=int(w_k-w)MA(u_i)+epsilon V, proving joint weighted continuity. Finite polarization transfers this from pure outputs to every mixed tuple; every subset-average net has the requisite finite-energy endpoint.

steps.claim: Genuine energy identity, affine unbounded calculus, reference and field covariance
steps.proof: Pass the continuous energy sum through the newly proved mixed weighted limit with u_i as weight and repeated u_i/reference slots. This gives the actual extended energy identity. Pass every coefficient in the continuous affine mixed polynomial identity separately using the full E1 weighted law; derivatives integrate v-u on a common finite-value full-measure set, never subtracting infinities. Absolute-majorant cocycle gives reference-class invariance, and the actual absolute continuous approximation nets identify the measure after changing reference. Complete-field pullback preserves continuous energy; decreasing energy gives E1 ascent/equality. Continuous mixed pushforward and weak limits give actual E1 mixed pushforward with unchanged raw V. No exact extension-supnorm equality or discrete-field rename.
